verses.text: So let's move beyond the basic teaching about Christ and grow toward maturity. We don't need to lay the foundation all over again: turning from dead works, faith in God,
teaching about baptisms, laying on of hands, resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
And we'll do this, if God allows.
Some people have once been enlightened, tasted the heavenly gift, shared in the Holy Spirit,
and tasted the goodness of God's word and the powers of the age to come,
but then fallen away. It's impossible to renew them to repentance again, since they are crucifying the Son of God all over again and exposing him to public disgrace.
Land that soaks up frequent rain and produces a crop useful to those who farm it receives God's blessing.
But land that grows thorns and weeds is worthless and close to being cursed; in the end it will be burned.
Even though we're speaking this way, dear friends, we're convinced better things are true of you—things that belong with salvation.
God isn't unjust. He won't forget your work and the love you've shown for his name by serving his people, as you still do.
We want each of you to show the same dedication, so your hope will be fully realized to the end.
Don't become lazy. Instead, imitate those who inherit God's promises through faith and patience.
When God made his promise to Abraham, he swore by himself, since there was no one greater to swear by.
He said, ‘I will surely bless you and make your descendants very numerous.’
After patiently waiting, Abraham received what God had promised.
People swear by someone greater than themselves, and an oath settles a dispute as a final confirmation.
God wanted to make the unchanging nature of his purpose especially clear to those who would inherit the promise, so he guaranteed it with an oath.
God did this so that, through two unchangeable things—in which it's impossible for God to lie—we who have fled to him for refuge would be strongly encouraged to hold on to the hope set before us.
We have this hope as a sure and steady anchor for our souls. It reaches behind the curtain into the inner sanctuary,
where Jesus has gone ahead of us as our forerunner. He became a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
